extracted.intended_audience: painters, artists, art students, and critics
extracted.subtask_description: Guiding principles for making and judging visual art (especially painting and mosaic) that emphasize expressive intent, symbolism, and the proper use of finish and medium-specific conventions. Rooted in Victorian-era art criticism but applicable as general aesthetic rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art's value as expression of the soul
rubrics_metrics.description: Art is valuable or otherwise, only as it expresses the personality, activity, and living perception of a good and great human soul; if it have not this, if it show not the vigor, perception, and invention of a mighty human spirit, it is worthless (as art).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An artwork may need little help from execution or science to be art; technical skill alone cannot make a work artistic. Examples: photographs or purely mechanical manipulations may be skilful but are not art in this highest sense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heart-work over hand-work and head-work
rubrics_metrics.description: The goodness of work is too often judged primarily by firmness of handling and accuracy of science (hand-work and head-work), whereas heart-work — the living feeling and perception — is the essential work we want.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not let teaching, patronage, or academic emphasis on finish and technical accuracy supplant cultivation of feeling, reverence, and inner perception. Technical finish without heart is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessity of the whole man being in his work
rubrics_metrics.description: The necessity of the whole man being in his work: the body must be in it (hands, habits), but chiefly the nobler part (heart, love, reverence, admiration) acting together with intellect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intellect alone is not noble; it becomes noble or ignoble according to the matter it deals with. The artist's whole being — sensibility + intellect + craft — should inform the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid pride in knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Take no pride in our knowledge; the increase of knowledge merely as such does not make the soul larger; one should not be proud of what has been taught by rote.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize openness of heart, clear perception, and lived experience rather than accumulation of technical facts. Example: a student who knows more facts than Giotto is not therefore nearer Giotto's artistic stature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symbolism preferred to direct imitation for noble art
rubrics_metrics.description: No art is noble which in any wise depends upon direct imitation for its effect upon the mind; symbolic expression that appeals to thought (not mere realization) is the only one allowable in noble art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use symbolic forms and conventional devices to address the mind and spirit. The Byzantine mosaics are cited as superior because they convey meaning under material constraints rather than attempting photographic realism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perception of distinguishing features (see the olive-tree example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Artists should feel and see the distinctive character of subjects (e.g., the olive-tree's greyish slender leaves, fibrous twisting stems, rounded downy foliage) rather than generalizing trees into a universal 'idea of a tree'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perception, not mere scientific fact, is required. Avoid reducing species-specific character to an abstract generality; show what makes a subject itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adapt representation to medium and decorative purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Representation must be adapted to the medium's constraints and purpose: e.g., a mosaicist working high in a dark cupola will stylize leaves into small clusters, render fruit as golden discs, and arrange symmetrically to suggest shape at distance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose scale, color, symmetry, and convention appropriate to viewing distance, material (glass tesserae, marble), and decorative function. Conventionalization is legitimate when it better conveys the idea within limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art must address and summon the whole being of the spectator
rubrics_metrics.description: All your faculties, all that is in you of greatest and best, must be awake in you, or I have no reward; the work must evoke senses, fancy, feeling, and reason together.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An artwork should call the spectator's whole attention; it is the artist's duty to evoke the highest faculties (especially imagination). If the work does not stir the whole person, it has failed in its primary duty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right point of realization: enable spectator to complete
rubrics_metrics.description: The right point of realization for any work is that which will enable the spectator to complete it for himself, in the exact way the artist would have him, but not that which will save him the trouble of effecting the completion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cease adding detail once the idea is conveyed sufficiently for the spectator's imagination to finish it. Over-realization robs the spectator of imaginative engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finish should add ideas, not merely substantiate
rubrics_metrics.description: All true finish consists in the addition of ideas; whenever finish is given for the sake of realization it is wrong; whenever it is given for the sake of adding ideas it is right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use finishing touches to introduce new suggestive information (clusters, acorns, gilded edges) that feed imagination. Finish used solely to imitate reality (to substantiate) insults the imagination (example: Hobbima's exhaustive realism versus Reynolds' suggestive dashes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantity of finish depends on number and kind of ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: The quantity of finish or detail which may rightly be bestowed upon any work depends on the number and kind of ideas which the artist wishes to convey, much more than on the amount of realization necessary to enable the imagination to grasp them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan detail according to communicative aims: complex ideas may justify more finish; simple suggestions may require less. Also allow for differences in viewers' imaginative powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid impertinent, non-suggestive detail
rubrics_metrics.description: The artist is infinitely to be blamed who insults the summoned imagination by putting anything into his work which is not suggestive; whatever he does merely to realize and substantiate an idea is impertinent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclude details the spectator already anticipates or that do not add imaginative food; avoid dwelling on particulars that detract from the evocative power of the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guide the imagination authoritatively without stifling it
rubrics_metrics.description: The guidance which the artist gives should be full and authoritative: the beholder's imagination must not be suffered to take its own way, or wander hither and thither; but neither must it be left at rest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide precise hints (a fully drawn cluster or a single bird) that direct the spectator's imaginative completion in the artist's intended manner, balancing direction and freedom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attend to essential/substantial features over trivialities
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not be intensely solicitous about trivial, verbal, external, or accidental matters (logic, rhetoric, perspective) while neglecting what is essential and substantial (the nature and distinctive character of the subject).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize things a spectator perceives as important (species-identifying traits, symbolic meaning) rather than only technical correctness of secondary matters (mathematical diminution at distance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanical manipulation alone is not art
rubrics_metrics.description: A photograph is not a work of art, though it requires delicate manipulation; nor would a drawing like a photograph, made directly from nature, be a work of art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat instruments and techniques as servants of the inner life and perception; the presence and expression of the inner man make the difference between craft/skill and art.
